chunks: And it was narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said:

I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a woman who was afflicted with drinking nabīdh, so she became intoxicated and married herself to a man while in her intoxication. Then she recovered and denied that; then she thought that it might be binding upon her, so she acted cautiously regarding it, and she remained with the man upon that marriage. Is it halal for her, or is the marriage invalid because of the intoxication, such that the man has no claim over her?
So he said: “If she remained with him after she recovered, then that is her consent.” I said: “And is that marriage valid upon her?” He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.السُّكْرِ: intoxication, the state affecting legal capacity in the case
key_terms.رِضَاهَا: her consent, established by remaining with him after sobriety
key_terms.فَزَوَّجَتْ: she married herself in contract to a man
key_terms.نَبِيذٍ: an intoxicating drink mentioned here as the cause of drunkenness

ai.seo_question: Is a marriage contracted while intoxicated valid if the woman later accepts it after becoming sober?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal status of a marriage contract initiated by a woman while intoxicated. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that if, after regaining sobriety, she remains with the man, that continued cohabitation counts as her consent and the marriage is valid.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4430 - Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi reported that he asked Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as), about a woman who had been afflicted with drinking wine and became intoxicated, then married herself to a man while in her intoxicated state.

When she sobered up, she denied it but then assumed that the marriage might be binding, so she remained with the man out of caution based on that marriage.
He asked whether this was lawful for her or if the marriage was invalid due to the intoxication, and whether the man had any claim over her.

Imam (as) said: "If she remained with him after she sobered up, then that is her consent."
He then asked: "Does such a marriage become valid for her?"
Imam (as) replied: "Yes."
